_comment: Curated official macro calendar, H2-2026, all times UTC. Entries with "estimated": true follow the usual publication pattern (CPI mid-month ~08:30 ET, Employment Situation first Friday ~08:30 ET, BEA GDP ~08:30 ET) and MUST be reviewed by the owner against the official schedules in each entry's _source before relying on them (see runbook). Never put release values here; values are collected from the official APIs or entered manually for BEA/FOMC.
_consensus_comment: "consensus_by_variable" is the FORECAST of a release, not its value, and it is keyed by the model variable because one release publishes several: the CPI report carries cpi_yoy, cpi_mom and core_cpi_yoy at once, and a flat number could not say which scale it is on. Every value MUST come from an official publisher and MUST carry "_consensus_source" with the URL and the date it was read — never our own estimate. An entry with no such source simply has no consensus and macro_scheduled abstains on its markets, which is the correct behaviour and not a bug. Nowcasts age: see docs/runbooks/polymarket-fundamental.md for when and how the owner refreshes them.

_consensus_absent.cpi-2026-10, cpi-2026-11, cpi-2026-12: The Cleveland Fed nowcasts only the CURRENT period — on 2026-08-31 the tables carried August 2026 and 2026:Q3 and nothing further out. These entries get a consensus when their data month becomes the current one.
_consensus_absent.nfp-*: No official publisher of a payrolls or unemployment-rate consensus is named in RFC-010 or the handoff, and the Cleveland Fed nowcasts prices only. Left without consensus rather than sourced from a vendor survey we cannot cite.
_consensus_absent.fomc-*: CME FedWatch publishes a probability distribution over 25bp TARGET RANGES, not a level with a dispersion. Collapsing it into the normal this model centres on a consensus would misstate its shape — on 2026-08-31 it was bimodal, ~66% at 3.75-4.00% and ~34% at 3.50-3.75%, with no mass at the mean of the two. Reading a level out of it would be our estimate, not the publisher's number.
_consensus_absent.gdp-*: BEA GDP is not a variable of macro_scheduled 1.0.0, so a consensus here would never be read. Calendar-only, as RFC-007 records it.

_consensus_source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland — Inflation Nowcasting
_consensus_source.nowcast_for: August 2026 data month, which is what this release publishes
_consensus_source.note: Headline CPI and core CPI, month-over-month and year-over-year, read from the published nowcast tables. The publisher states no dispersion for these nowcasts, so consensus_std is deliberately absent and the model falls back to macro.default_sigma. core_cpi_mom (0.20 on the same table) is omitted because it is not a variable of macro_scheduled 1.0.0.
